# q and q̃ — formal definition and mixture map (Wintenberger–Shepherd)

*Generated by `src/cycles/q_mapping.py` on 2026-08-19; inputs from `data/cycles_ws.json` (Cantera 3.2 + SD Toolbox, stoichiometric mixtures at 300 K, 1 bar). Slide-ready.*

## Formal statement (five lines)

1. **Definition (Paper B, Eq. 1).** q_c ≡ h₁(T₁,P₁) − h₆(T₁,P₁): specific heat of combustion = enthalpy of the reactants minus enthalpy of the **equilibrium products at the same initial state** (T₁, P₁), per unit mass of mixture. At 300 K the equilibrium products are the major species (CO₂, H₂O vapour, N₂), so q_c equals the formation-enthalpy (lower-heating-value) heat release: max deviation across the 12 mixtures 0.00%. Standard-state precision (2026-07-09, `validation/q_formal.md`): the *formal* heat release is anchored to T_ref = 298.15 K, q° ≡ Σᵢ Y_i,1 Δh°f,i(T_ref) − Σᵢ Y_i,2 Δh°f,i(T_ref); exactly q_c(T₁) = q° + ∫_{T_ref}^{T₁}(c_p,react − c_p,prod)dT′, so the q_c of this table (T₁ = 300 K) differs from q° only by the sensible shift q° − q_c = −0.0076 % (H₂–air) / +0.0023 % (CH₄–air) — percent-grade only at preheated T₁ (700 K, same q°−q_c convention: −1.58 %/+0.30 %); the 300 K values below are unaffected.
2. **Non-dimensionalization.** The papers use q̃ = q_c/(c_p T₁) on the classical Hugoniot and in the FJ closed form (Eqs. A18/A21, B2–B3), q̃_t = q_c/(c_p T_t1) on the stagnation Hugoniot (A40–A42, existence limit q̃_t < 1/(γ²−1)), and q_c/(R T₁) = γ/(γ−1)·q̃ as the family label of Fig. A22.
3. **CJ Mach number (Eq. B2).** M_CJ = √(H+1) + √H with H = (γ²−1) q_c/(2γRT₂) = (γ+1)/2 · q_c/(c_p T₂), T₂ = temperature of the (possibly precompressed) reactants ahead of the wave.
4. **Exact inverse.** H = (M_CJ²−1)²/(4M_CJ²), hence **q̃ = q_c/(c_p T₁) = (M_CJ²−1)²/(2(γ+1)M_CJ²)** and q_c/(RT₁) = γ(M_CJ²−1)²/(2(γ²−1)M_CJ²). Check on the spec §3.1 benchmark: γ=1.4, q̃=4 → M_CJ=4.599 → q̃ back to 4.000.
5. **Effective heat release.** q_eff = inverse formula at the physical M_CJ (CJ speed over frozen reactant sound speed) with γ = γ_e(CJ) of the products: for fuel–O₂, q_eff < q_c — dissociation withholds part of the release (the paper’s mechanism for the low fuel–O₂ η); for fuel–air, q_eff mildly exceeds q_c because M_CJ is referenced to the reactants’ sound speed (γ₁≈1.39) while the one-γ model implies a₁=√(γ_e RT₁) — see `validation/gamma_phase_audit.md`.

## Traceability of the Fig. A22 family (`fig_cycle_family`, γ = 1.2)

Curve labels are q_c/RT₁; nearest stoichiometric mixtures by their actual q_c/RT₁ (γ=1.2 model reproduces their M_CJ to 3.8% max across fuel–air, asserted <5% in this script):

- **q_c/RT₁ = 10** ↔ — (no stoichiometric mixture this low; lean fuel–air territory)
- **q_c/RT₁ = 20** ↔ — (no stoichiometric mixture this low; lean fuel–air territory)
- **q_c/RT₁ = 30** ↔ CH4/air (30.6), H2/air (28.7)
- **q_c/RT₁ = 40** ↔ C2H2/air (39.1)
- fuel–O₂ mixtures lie far above the family (q_c/RT₁ = 65–156) and have γ_e ≈ 1.13, not 1.2: the family is a fuel–air-class model.
